title: Volume of Prisms and Cylinders — Problems

problems.problem_text: Find the volume of a cuboid with length 6 cm, width 5 cm, and height 4 cm.
problems.solution: V = l x w x h = 6 x 5 x 4 = 120 cm^3

problems.problem_text: Find the volume of a cube with side length 7 cm.
Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 4 cm and height 10 cm (use pi = 3.142).
A triangular prism has triangular cross-section with base 8 cm and height 5 cm, and length 12 cm. Find its volume.
problems.solution: Area of triangle = (1/2) x 8 x 5 = 20 cm^2. V = 20 x 12 = 240 cm^3

problems.problem_text: A cuboid has volume 360 cm^3, length 12 cm, and width 5 cm. Find its height.
problems.solution: V = l x w x h. 360 = 12 x 5 x h. 360 = 60h. h = 6 cm

problems.problem_text: A rectangular tank measures 50 cm by 30 cm by 40 cm. How many litres of water can it hold? (1 litre = 1000 cm^3)
A cylinder has diameter 14 cm and height 20 cm. Find its volume (use pi = 22/7).
A prism has cross-sectional area 25 cm^2 and length 9 cm. Find its volume.
problems.solution: V = area of cross-section x length = 25 x 9 = 225 cm^3

problems.problem_text: A cylindrical water tank has radius 30 cm and height 100 cm. How many litres does it hold? (pi = 3.142, 1 L = 1000 cm^3)
A swimming pool is 25 m long, 10 m wide, and has an average depth of 1.5 m. Find its volume in m^3.
A cylinder has volume 1000 cm^3 and height 12 cm. Find its radius (use pi = 3.142).
A cylinder of radius 6 cm and height 12 cm has a hemisphere of the same radius removed from the top. Find the remaining volume (use pi = 3.142).
A prism has cross-sectional area (3x+2) cm^2 and length (x+4) cm. Find an expression for its volume.
A prism has a trapezium cross-section with parallel sides 5 cm and 9 cm, height 4 cm, and prism length 10 cm. Find its volume.
problems.solution: Area of trapezium = (1/2)(5+9) x 4 = 28 cm^2. V = 28 x 10 = 280 cm^3

problems.problem_text: A cylindrical barrel of radius 30 cm contains water to a depth of 40 cm. How many litres of water are in the barrel? (pi = 3.142, 1 L = 1000 cm^3)
